title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. Every position discussed below is paper, and a single trade says nothing about a strategy. The record is a reading of engine state at one moment, not a verdict on any method.

## What the engines report

htf-rsi-v007 reports 0 positions open on paper and 4 closed trades so far, with average null net per trade. trend-daily-v005 reports the Bitcoin market filter off, 0 positions open on paper, and 6 closed trades so far, with average -13.22% net per trade. trend-daily-v006 reports the Bitcoin market filter off, 0 positions open on paper, and 7 closed trades so far, with average -13.34% net per trade. These are the engines' own counts and averages, read from the running record. The snapshot itself was read at 2026-11-16T03:12:30.120Z. Because the record updates continuously, a later read can show different counts, different averages, or a changed filter state. Nothing in this snapshot should be treated as a fixed conclusion about either engine. The performance page, signal log, and channel status carry the same counts, so the figures are not unique to this article.

## Open positions and recent closed trades

The open position is NEAR: an entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since. The first live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close; that position exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is −17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. The ATOM exit below its 10-day low is a rule-based close at the daily close, reported with its entry, exit, and percentage after the 30 bps round trip. The live record for v005 counts from 1 October 2026, and the live record for v006 counts from 9 October 2026. Those dates matter because they define which trades belong to the live record rather than to any earlier testing record. The ATOM result is one closed trade with a stated percentage after costs; it is not, by itself, evidence about the quality of either trend engine. NEAR remains open, so its outcome is not yet in the closed-trade averages. Until it closes, the open position is simply an entry price and a date in the record, not a realized result.

## Market filter and breakout distances

For trend-daily-v005 and trend-daily-v006, the Bitcoin market filter is off and both engines show 0 positions open on paper. The names closest to their 20-day breakout are reported as distances below their highs: for v005, TRXUSDT is 13.34% below its high, XLMUSDT is 17.87% below its high, and AVAXUSDT is 18.82% below its high; for v006, JUPUSDT is 5.46% below its high, TRXUSDT is 13.34% below its high, and XLMUSDT is 17.87% below its high. These are measurements of where each name stands relative to its 20-day high at the snapshot. They are not entry signals, and they do not imply that any name will break out. A filter that is off means the engines are not opening positions under that filter state; the distances still describe the market list, but they do not override the filter state. The same distance can be read as a gap to a breakout level, while the filter state determines whether that gap is actionable in the engine's own rules. JUPUSDT at 5.46% is closer to its high than TRXUSDT at 13.34%, which is closer than XLMUSDT at 17.87%.

## How to read this record

The closed-trade averages are negative for both trend-daily engines: -13.22% net per trade across 6 trades for v005 and -13.34% net per trade across 7 trades for v006. htf-rsi-v007 has 4 closed trades with average null net per trade. The average null net per trade for htf-rsi-v007 means the reported average is null, not a percentage comparable to the trend-daily averages. In testing, losses were more common than wins and the average winner was roughly +19%, so a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. That expectation provides context for reading a small live sample; it is not a prediction about these engines and it does not convert the current record into a forecast. The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. Paper signals only; no real orders are placed anywhere in this record. The record updates continuously, and the counts, averages, open positions, and distance-to-breakout figures should be read as the state at the snapshot time, not as a fixed conclusion.
